title: The roles and the rules for combining them
blurb: Describe the executive, senior user, senior supplier, project manager and team manager roles, and apply the rules for combining and sharing them.
question: A small charity wants its operations director to act as both executive and project manager. Is this allowed in PRINCE2?

teach.body: Formally: PRINCE2 defines roles with responsibilities, not job titles. One person may hold more than one role, and some roles may be shared by several people, within a few firm rules. In plain English: map the people you have onto the roles the project needs, but never break the rules that protect accountability, such as having one executive who is not also the project manager.

teach.h: The main roles at a glance
head: Role
Key responsibilities
Holders
rows: Single point of accountability; secures funding; owns business case
User requirements, benefits, handover and adoption
Supplier resources; supplier product quality; technical integrity
Runs the project day to day for the board; sets WP tolerances
Delivers products to specification within tolerances
teach.caption: Every role also carries v7 duties for safety, well-being and sustainability at its own level.

teach.body: Appointed by the business as the single point of accountability, the executive is ultimately accountable for the project's success, and that accountability cannot be delegated. The executive secures funding, is responsible for the business case and continued business justification, and governs in line with business strategy, including longer-term environmental, social and economic impacts.

teach.h: Can these be combined or shared?
head: Arrangement
Allowed?
Reason
rows: PM also acts as team manager
Depends on scale, complexity, skill, capacity
Assurance is independent of the PM
teach.caption: The PM role should not be shared: it needs a single focus.

teach.h: Quick decision: combining or sharing a role
Executive versus senior user on benefits
teach.caption: The senior user's commitment can extend beyond the project, for example to realize benefits.

teach.h: Worked scenario: a credit union app
teach.body: Northgate Credit Union's chief executive calls herself 'sponsor' of a new mobile app. In PRINCE2 terms she sits in the business layer and names chief operating officer Hamid Rahman as executive. Head of member services Lucy Tran is senior user; the app studio's director, Paul Okafor, is senior supplier. On this small project, project manager Dina Cole also acts as team manager and does her own project support. Nobody holds both the executive and project manager roles.

teach.text: Traps: (1) 'Sponsor' is not a PRINCE2 role: map it to the executive or the business layer. (2) The PM may take on team manager and project support, but never executive or project assurance. (3) The executive can delegate work, but not accountability for the project's success.

items: PRINCE2 assigns roles, not jobs; one person can hold several roles.
One executive, not combined with the PM; executive accountability cannot be delegated.
Senior user and senior supplier may be several people.
PM should not be shared; may also be team manager and project support.

summary: You can now describe the responsibilities of the executive, senior user, senior supplier, project manager and team manager. You can also say which roles may be combined or shared and which never can.

A.q: How many people can hold the executive role on a PRINCE2 project?
A.why: There cannot be more than one executive (6.2.4).

whyNot.0: The executive role cannot be shared between two people.
whyNot.2: The executive stays the single point of accountability for the whole project, not per stage.
whyNot.3: The executive represents the business interest; users and suppliers have their own roles.

A.q: Depending on scale and capacity, which roles may the project manager also perform?
A.why: Depending on scale, complexity, skill and capacity, the PM may also perform the team manager and project support roles.

whyNot.0: The executive role cannot be combined with the project manager.
whyNot.1: Project assurance cannot be assigned to the project manager.
whyNot.3: The senior user is a board role representing users; the rule allows team manager and support.

A.q: Which role is accountable for capturing user requirements and specifying the benefits?
A.why: The senior user is accountable for the approach to capturing user requirements and for specifying benefits aligned to the business case.

whyNot.0: The executive owns the business case and continued justification.
whyNot.1: The senior supplier represents those delivering the products.
whyNot.2: The project manager manages day to day; accountability for requirements sits with the senior user.

B.q:
Which two statements about PRINCE2 roles are correct?
1. One person can hold more than one PRINCE2 role.
2. The executive may delegate accountability for success to the PM.
3. The senior supplier role may be held by several people.
4. On large projects the PM role should be shared between two people.
B.why: PRINCE2 assigns roles, not jobs, so one person can hold several (1), and the senior supplier may be more than one person (3).

whyNot.1: Statement 2 is false: the executive's accountability cannot be delegated.
whyNot.2: Both are false: accountability stays with the executive, and the PM role should not be shared.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: the PM role should not be shared.

B.q: Which role is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and for the project's technical integrity?
B.why: The senior supplier is accountable for the quality of products delivered by suppliers and for technical integrity.

whyNot.0: The senior user represents users and their requirements.
whyNot.2: The team manager delivers products to specification but is not accountable for supplier quality overall.
whyNot.3: The executive is accountable for the project's success and the business case.

B.q: A company names its finance director as project 'sponsor'. How does PRINCE2 treat this?
options: The sponsor is added as a fourth board role
The sponsor takes on the role of senior user
The sponsor takes over as project manager
The sponsor becomes or sits above the executive
B.why: PRINCE2 has no sponsor role; a sponsor typically becomes the executive or sits above it in the business layer.

whyNot.0: The board has three roles: executive, senior user and senior supplier.
whyNot.1: The senior user represents users; a sponsor backs the investment, which is the business side.
whyNot.2: A sponsor is a senior figure, not the day-to-day project manager.

C.q: Which role secures funding for the project, and can that role also act as project manager?
C.why: The executive secures funding, and the executive role cannot be combined with the project manager role.

whyNot.1: The role is right, but the combination is not allowed on any size of project.
whyNot.2: The senior user specifies benefits; the executive secures funding.
whyNot.3: The project manager does not secure funding.

C.q: Which role delivers products to the agreed specifications, and who sets its tolerances?
C.why: The team manager delivers products to specification within tolerances and constraints agreed with the project manager.

whyNot.0: The board sets stage tolerances; work package tolerances come from the PM.
whyNot.1: The senior supplier commits resources at board level; team managers deliver.
whyNot.3: This is reversed: the PM sets tolerances for the team manager.

C.q: Which role is responsible for successful handover and adoption of products, and can that commitment extend beyond closure?
C.why: The senior user is responsible for handover and adoption and must secure ongoing commitment from users, including after closure, for example to realize benefits.

whyNot.0: The executive owns the business case; handover and adoption are the senior user's.
whyNot.1: The role is right, but the senior user's commitment can extend beyond the project.
whyNot.2: The senior supplier delivers the products; adoption by users is the senior user's.

reteach.title: A football club: owner, fans, kit maker, manager
reteach.question: At a club, can the owner also be the team's manager? And can there be two owners on the final say?

blocks.body: The owner answers for the club's success and funds it (executive). The supporters' representative speaks for those who use the stadium (senior user). The kit maker's director speaks for the supplier (senior supplier). The manager runs things day to day (project manager) and, at a small club, may also coach and do the admin. PRINCE2 keeps one rule firm: the person who answers for the investment is not the one running it day to day.

blocks.text: Executive accountability cannot be handed to the project manager, however capable the PM is.

explain.body: PRINCE2 assigns roles. One person can hold several roles, and some roles can be shared, within the rules.

test.q: Which statement about PRINCE2 roles is correct?
options: Each role needs a different person
Roles must match people's job titles
A person may hold more than one role
The executive role may be shared
test.why: PRINCE2 defines roles, not jobs, so one person can hold several roles within the rules.

whyNot.0: Roles can be combined, for example PM and team manager.
whyNot.1: Roles are independent of job titles in the organization.
whyNot.3: There can be only one executive.

explain.body: The executive is the single point of accountability for the project. This accountability cannot be delegated. The executive secures funding and owns the business case.

test.q: Which is true of the executive's accountability for the project's success?
options: It passes to the PM day to day
It is shared with the senior user
test.why: The executive is ultimately accountable for success and this accountability cannot be delegated.

whyNot.0: The PM manages day to day on the board's behalf; accountability stays with the executive.
whyNot.1: The executive is the single point of accountability.
whyNot.2: The executive remains accountable throughout the project.

explain.body: The senior user represents users, requirements and benefits. The senior supplier represents suppliers, commits their people and resources, and is accountable for supplier product quality and technical integrity.

test.q: Which role commits supplier people and resources to the project?
test.why: The senior supplier must ensure sufficient ongoing commitment of supplier people and resources.

whyNot.1: The senior user commits user resources, not supplier ones.
whyNot.2: The executive secures funding; supplier resources are the senior supplier's.
whyNot.3: Team managers use the resources allocated to their work packages.

explain.body: The PM runs the project day to day on behalf of the board. The PM role should not be shared, but depending on scale, complexity, skill and capacity the PM may also perform the team manager and project support roles.

test.q: According to PRINCE2, which role may also perform the team manager role, depending on scale and capacity?
test.why: The PM may also perform the team manager and project support roles.

whyNot.0: The executive directs at board level; the rule names the PM.
whyNot.2: Project assurance must stay independent of day-to-day delivery and the PM.
whyNot.3: The business layer commissions the project from outside the PMT.
